title: Shapes and colours of the Moon
paragraphs: You may have heard of the idiom 'once in a blue moon' to describe an event that doesn't happen often. But can the Moon really be blue? Our closest neighbour in this vast galaxy, the Moon, orbits the Earth like a natural satellite. Unlike many of the other planets in our Solar System, ours only has the one moon. If you flew to it, you would land on grey rocks. This is because the lunar surface is made from mostly magnesium, iron and other minerals of that colour. But, if you're lucky to have clear skies under the curtain of night, you may be able to admire its luminosity. You might even see that it seems to change shape and hue.

It's important to understand that the Moon reflects light from the Sun as it orbits the Earth, and that light bounces back to the Earth. The position of the Moon, Sun and the Earth determines how much of the Moon we see. The new Moon appears almost invisible in the sky as it is in total darkness. This is the opposite to the full Moon which is completely lit up. There are eight different phases to the lunar cycle between a full Moon and a new Moon, each lasting around 28 days. In fact, the word 'month' takes its root from 'Moon' because it was almost equal to the lunar phases.

The other phases include the crescent, quarter and gibbous phase. Crescent originates from the Latin verb 'crescere', meaning 'to increase', and so it is the phase just before and after a new Moon as it takes a concave shape. The quarter will show half of the Moon. 'Gibbous' gets its root from the Latin term 'gibbous' which applied to the Moon's convex shape. These shapes are determined by the adjectives 'waning', to get smaller, and 'waxing', to get bigger.

So now you know how we've named the shapes, what about those mesmerising colours? The light waves that reach our eyes can vary due to the Moon's position on the horizon and pollution. This is known as Rayleigh scattering. When the Moon is low, light travels through the densest part of the atmosphere and shorter waves of blue scatter away. This leaves only the red and orange light waves to reach us. A warmer atmosphere, as well as smoke from wildfire, may increase the scattering effect as well, making the Moon appear less dull in spring and summer. This is why it's more likely for you to look up and see a pink Moon in April, a golden Moon in May and July, and even a red coloured Moon in the month of June.
chineseParagraphs: 你可能听过习语千载难逢来形容不常发生的事件。但月亮真的会是蓝色的吗？月球是我们在这广阔银河系中最近的邻居，像一颗天然卫星一样绕地球运行。与我们太阳系中的许多其他行星不同，我们的地球只有这一颗卫星。如果你飞往月球，你会降落在灰色的岩石上。这是因为月球表面主要由镁、铁和其他灰色矿物质构成。但是，如果你幸运地在夜幕下拥有晴朗的天空，你或许能欣赏到它的光辉。你甚至可能看到它的形状和色调似乎在变化。
重要的是要知道，月球在绕地球运行时反射来自太阳的光，光再弹回地球。月球、太阳和地球的位置决定了我们看到月球的多少。新月在天空中几乎看不见，因为它完全处于黑暗中。这与完全被照亮的满月相反。从满月到新月之间，月相周期有八个不同的阶段，每个阶段持续大约28天。事实上，“月份”（month）这个词的词根就来自“月亮”（Moon），因为它几乎等同于月相周期。
其他月相包括蛾眉月、弦月和凸月。“Crescent”源自拉丁动词“crescere”，意为“增加”，因此它指的是新月前后呈现凹形的阶段。“弦月”会显示月亮的一半。“Gibbous”（凸月）的词根来自拉丁语“gibbous”，用于描述月亮凸起的形状。这些形状由形容词“waning”（渐亏，变小）和“waxing”（渐盈，变大）来确定。

现在你知道了我们如何命名月亮的形状，那那些迷人的色彩呢？到达我们眼睛的光波会因月亮在地平线上的位置和污染而变化。这被称为瑞利散射。当月亮位置较低时，光线穿过大气层最稠密的部分，较短的蓝色光波被散射掉。只留下红色和橙色的光波到达我们眼中。较温暖的大气层以及野火产生的烟雾也可能增加散射效应，使月亮在春季和夏季看起来不那么暗淡。这就是为什么你在四月更可能看到粉色的月亮，在五月和七月看到金色的月亮，甚至在六月看到红色的月亮。

vocabulary.entry: idiom /ˈɪdiəm/ n. 习语，成语
vocabulary.example: “Once in a blue moon” is a common English idiom.
vocabulary.translation: “千载难逢”是一个常见的英语习语。

vocabulary.definition: 千载难逢地，极少地（固定表达）
vocabulary.entry: once in a blue moon /ˌwʌns ɪn ə bluː ˈmuːn/ phr. 千载难逢地，极少地（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: He visits his parents once in a blue moon.
vocabulary.translation: 他难得去看望父母一次。

vocabulary.entry: galaxy /ˈɡæləksi/ n. 星系（专业术语）
vocabulary.example: The Milky Way is the galaxy that contains our Solar System.
vocabulary.translation: 银河系是包含我们太阳系的星系。

vocabulary.entry: orbit /ˈɔːbɪt/ v. 绕……轨道运行（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The satellite orbits the Earth every 90 minutes.
vocabulary.translation: 这颗卫星每90分钟绕地球一周。

vocabulary.entry: satellite /ˈsætəlaɪt/ n. 卫星
vocabulary.example: The moon is a natural satellite of the Earth.
vocabulary.translation: 月球是地球的一颗天然卫星。

vocabulary.entry: Solar System /ˈsəʊlə ˌsɪstəm/ n. 太阳系（固定表达）
vocabulary.example: There are eight planets in our Solar System.
vocabulary.translation: 我们的太阳系中有八颗行星。

vocabulary.definition: 月球的，月亮的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.entry: lunar /ˈluːnə(r)/ adj. 月球的，月亮的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The lunar surface is covered with craters.
vocabulary.translation: 月球表面布满了陨石坑。

vocabulary.entry: magnesium /mæɡˈniːziəm/ n. 镁（化学元素，专业术语）
vocabulary.example: Magnesium is an important mineral for the body.
vocabulary.translation: 镁是人体重要的矿物质。

vocabulary.entry: mineral /ˈmɪnərəl/ n. 矿物质
vocabulary.example: The water contains important minerals like calcium and magnesium.
vocabulary.translation: 这种水含有钙和镁等重要矿物质。

vocabulary.entry: luminosity /ˌluːmɪˈnɒsəti/ n. 发光性，亮度（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The luminosity of the stars was breathtaking.
vocabulary.translation: 星星的亮度令人叹为观止。

vocabulary.entry: hue /hjuː/ n. 色调，色度（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The room was decorated in hues of blue and green.
vocabulary.translation: 房间装饰成蓝色和绿色的色调。

vocabulary.entry: phase /feɪz/ n. 阶段，时期；（月相）
vocabulary.example: The project is in its final phase.
vocabulary.translation: 该项目正处于最后阶段。

vocabulary.entry: crescent /ˈkresnt/ n. 蛾眉月，新月形
vocabulary.example: The moon was a thin crescent in the sky.
vocabulary.translation: 天空中的月亮是一弯蛾眉月。

vocabulary.entry: originate /əˈrɪdʒɪneɪt/ v. 起源，发源（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The game is thought to have originated in Europe.
vocabulary.translation: 这种游戏被认为起源于欧洲。

vocabulary.entry: concave /ˈkɒnkeɪv/ adj. 凹的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The inside of the bowl is concave.
vocabulary.translation: 碗的内侧是凹的。

vocabulary.entry: convex /ˈkɒnveks/ adj. 凸的（专业术语，书面语）
vocabulary.example: The lens is convex on both sides.
vocabulary.translation: 这个镜片两面都是凸的。

vocabulary.entry: waning /ˈweɪnɪŋ/ adj. 渐亏的，衰退的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The moon was in its waning phase.
vocabulary.translation: 月亮正处于渐亏阶段。

vocabulary.entry: waxing /ˈwæksɪŋ/ adj. 渐盈的，增长的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The moon is waxing towards fullness.
vocabulary.translation: 月亮正朝着满月渐盈。

vocabulary.definition: 令人着迷的，引人入胜的（书面语）
vocabulary.entry: mesmerising /ˈmezməraɪzɪŋ/ adj. 令人着迷的，引人入胜的（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The view from the top was mesmerising.
vocabulary.translation: 山顶的景色令人着迷。

vocabulary.entry: horizon /həˈraɪzn/ n. 地平线
vocabulary.example: The sun sank below the horizon.
vocabulary.translation: 太阳落到了地平线以下。

vocabulary.entry: Rayleigh scattering /ˈreɪli ˈskætərɪŋ/ n. 瑞利散射（物理学术语）
vocabulary.example: Rayleigh scattering explains why the sky is blue.
vocabulary.translation: 瑞利散射解释了为什么天空是蓝色的。

vocabulary.entry: scatter /ˈskætə(r)/ v. 散开，分散（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The birds scattered when they heard the noise.
vocabulary.translation: 鸟儿听到声音后四处飞散。

vocabulary.entry: dense /dens/ adj. 密集的，浓密的
vocabulary.example: The forest was so dense that we could barely see the sky.
vocabulary.translation: 森林如此茂密，我们几乎看不到天空。

vocabulary.entry: atmosphere /ˈætməsfɪə(r)/ n. 大气，大气层
vocabulary.example: The spacecraft re-entered the Earth's atmosphere.
vocabulary.translation: 宇宙飞船重新进入了地球大气层。

vocabulary.entry: wildfire /ˈwaɪldfaɪə(r)/ n. 野火
vocabulary.example: The dry summer has increased the risk of wildfires.
vocabulary.translation: 干燥的夏季增加了发生野火的风险。

vocabulary.entry: dull /dʌl/ adj. 暗淡的，乏味的
vocabulary.example: The sky was dull and grey.
vocabulary.translation: 天空阴沉灰暗。
